generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, this runs through every essay and lab report you write. When you cite a study on memory or a theory of development, three things happen at once. You hold the values, you choose the reference with purpose, and you judge whether to quote a definition or paraphrase a finding. A reference list on, say, attachment research shows a reader both your reading and your judgement at once.
generatedProse.worked-example: A psychology student is writing up a study on bystander behaviour. At first they lift the author's polished sentence, swap a word or two, and add a citation, which still leaves the phrasing the source's own. On reflection they set the source aside, restate the finding in plain words, and cite it to credit the researcher and show where it sits in the debate. The paragraph now shows understanding, and the reference does real work in the argument.
generatedProse.summary: In psychology, using sources with integrity is one practice you repeat across every essay and report. With each study you cite, you hold the values, reference with purpose, and judge how to quote or paraphrase it. That habit, not any single citation, is what makes your psychology writing trustworthy.

check.body: A student weighs whether to quote or paraphrase a source. They rework it in their own words, because the idea matters more than the wording, and reference it to credit the author and show their reading. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following report improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next report, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next report improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: Integrity working as one practice: the values, the reasons for referencing, and the judgement about using the source are all in play at once.
_items.feedback: Yes. The student held the values, referenced with purpose, and judged how to use the source, together.

_items.text: That the student quoted the source directly to keep its exact wording.
_items.feedback: They paraphrased, judging that the idea mattered more than the wording.

_items.text: That referencing is only about avoiding plagiarism.
_items.feedback: The reference here also credits the author and shows the student's reading.

_items.text: That the values and the judgement are separate from the reference.
_items.feedback: The reference is where the values and the judgement become visible; they are not separate.
